Q: How to run multiple OS simultaneously on different cores of ARMv8 A:

That's a very-very vague question, so answer gonna be the same sort.

That's how ARMv8 looks like.

Is it possible to run the following OSs simultaneously?

Yes, there should not be restrictions for that.

All of them use some shared memory space to exchange data.

Yes, you could map same region of physical memory to all of them. How to sync access to that shared memory from different OSs (eg isolated from each other environments) is more important question though.

Boot sequences until loading image(monolithic RTOS and Linux kernel) into DDR are processed by external chip.

For sure you should have an image of OS in memory before passing control to Kernel entry. So should be done from EL3 or EL2.

Do I need to use a hypervisor, or just treat all cores as independent logical CPUs?

Yes, you do need hypervisor. That's probably the best way to organise interaction between different OSs.

should I pay additional attentions in setting MMU, GIC, etc. in my case?

There are MMU for each EL. So MMU-EL0 are totally independent. MMU-EL1 (OS/Kernel) to organise interaction between App in same OS. MMU-EL2 (hypervisor) to organise interaction between different OS. But all in all probably not something special.

GIC, that's depends on how you are gonna organise interrupts. It's possible to route interrupts to all cores or only particular one. Use them to change EL and select which OS is gonna to handle it. So yes, GIC might need quite an attention.

Q: Flip an svg along the x-axis so it's upside down A:

Since 2022 you can use:

transform: rotateY(180deg)

and

transform: rotateX(180deg)

to flip along your desired axis

Q: Kernighan and Ritchie book. If the string does not contain a newline character, then the last character of the string will be removed. Is this a bug? A:

Yes, if it is not guaranteed that the input contains a newline character, then the line

line[len - 1] = '\0';

would indeed be a bug.

So whether this line is a bug or not depends on the environment in which the program runs.

If the program for example gets its input piped from a text file whose lines are guaranteed to always end with a newline character (including the last line), then this line of code is not a bug.

However, if the program gets its input from the user in a terminal window, and if it is possible for the user to send end-of-file in this terminal window (for example by pressing CTRL-D on Linux), then it is possible for the line to not have a newline character at the end. In that case, the line of code would indeed be a bug.

If you want the program to remove the newline character if it exists, but otherwise do nothing, then one thing you can do is to replace the line

line[len - 1] = '\0';

with:

line[strcspn(line,"\n")] = '\0';

That way, if the newline character exists, it will be overwritten with a null character, and if it doesn't exist, the null character will be overwritten with another null character (which effectively does nothing).

See the following question for further information:
Removing trailing newline character from fgets() input

Q: How to write an SQLAlchemy query to get a list of keys from a JSON column, but return it as a single list, not separate rows? A:

You can use a jsonpath expression:

stmt = sa.select(
    sa.func.jsonb_path_query_array(
        model.MyModel.extra_data, cast("$.keyvalue().key", JSONPATH)
    )
)

demo at db<>fiddle

select jsonb_path_query_array(extra_data,'$.keyvalue().key')
from t;
jsonb_path_query_array
["key1", "key2"]
["key3", "key4"]

It would help if you showed your attempts to use array_agg() and group by because that should work too.

One difference is that aggregating the key column from jsonb_object_keys() gets you a text[] array, while the jsonb_path_query_array() yields a jsonb with a JSON array of strings in it. I'm not sure how much, if at all, that changes how you pick them up in SQLAlchemy but at raw SQL level it's a meaningful difference.
